title: Qatar's MCIT Partners with SignQuantum on Post-Quantum Cybersecurity
html:
Insider Brief

  • Qatar’s Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) has signed a collaboration agreement with SignQuantum to assess post-quantum cybersecurity applications and prepare for risks associated with quantum computing.
  • The agreement covers knowledge sharing and the exploration of potential use cases for post-quantum cryptography and quantum-resistant digital signatures, with any pilots or deployments subject to separate approvals.
  • SignQuantum‘s solution combines post-quantum digital signatures with quantum-resistant timestamping through QANplatform’s blockchain technology to protect the integrity and authenticity of digital records.

PRESS RELEASE — The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology of the State of Qatar (MCIT Qatar) signed a collaboration agreement with SignQuantum to strengthen cybersecurity readiness for quantum computing risks. The announcement was made at MWC26 Doha on November 10, 2026.

“Qatar’s digital future must be built on trust that endures. Under the Qatar National Vision 2030 and the Digital Agenda 2030, our priority is to ensure that government services, digital transactions, and data remain secure, transparent, and resilient both today and for decades to come,” said Faraj Jassim Abdulla, Director of the Digital Economy Department, Ministry of Communications and Information Technology.

“This collaboration with SignQuantum reflects Qatar’s proactive approach to emerging cybersecurity threats, including those posed by quantum computing. It also underscores MCIT’s ongoing support for local startups and scale-ups, providing them with opportunities to engage with government stakeholders and explore potential use cases that support Qatar’s digital transformation objectives.” said Faraj Jassim Abdulla, Director of the Digital Economy Department, Ministry of Communications and Information Technology.

Under the agreement, MCIT and SignQuantum intend to share knowledge and explore potential use cases for post-quantum cryptography and quantum-resistant digital signatures. Any future pilot implementation, technology deployment or commercial engagement would be subject to separate evaluation, approvals and agreements.

SignQuantum is a self-hosted post-quantum business trust and continuity solution protecting digital documents, data, and authenticated transactions. It combines post-quantum signatures with mathematically provable, quantum-resistant time-stamping via QANplatform’s quantum-safe blockchain to preserve integrity and authenticity over time.
“Recent root certificate authority key compromises have shown us that trust cannot rest on digital signatures alone. Even post-quantum signatures need verifiable, tamper-evident anchoring to be trustworthy, and capable of mathematically proving authenticity. QANplatform is proud to expand by powering SignQuantum in Qatar’s public sector,” said Johann Polecsak, Co-Founder and CTO of QANplatform, Director of Blockchain Technology at MBK Holding.

“We are thrilled to see that SignQuantum, a member of MBK Holding, can contribute to the Qatar National Vision 2030 and the Digital Agenda 2030 with its post-quantum cybersecurity expertise,” said H.E. Sheikh Mansoor Bin Khalifa Al-Thani, Founder and Chairman of MBK Holding, and former director of information technology for The Council of The Qatar Ruling Family Affairs.

The announcement was made in Doha, Qatar, MWC26 Doha, held November 8–10, 2026, at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Center. MWC26 Doha was hosted by MCIT Qatar and organized by GSMA, the global organization representing over 1,000 mobile operators and businesses across the telecom and related industries. The event was co-located with ITU PP-26, the United Nations’ highest policy-making conference for digital technologies.

Mohib Ur Rehman

MENTIONED IN THE ARTICLE

SignQuantum is a software add-on developed by Quantum Software Solutions (a Qatari technology innovation and research lab under MBK Holding) which provides post-quantum security for digitally-signed, business-critical documents.
